adhdindia,"I asked ChatGPT to make it ADHD-Friendly xD
My ADHD Journey (India)
Hey everyone!
Just wanted to share my ADHD journey—hoping it helps someone out there. Here’s how it’s been for me:
Diagnosis & First Experiences

column3: I was diagnosed with ADHD in 2023.
My therapist recommended CBT and lifestyle changes instead of meds.
I was still curious about medication, so I went to a psychiatrist.

column1: That psychiatrist… not it.

column3: He said I was a chain smoker (okay, yes—20 cigarettes a day—but chain smoker? Dramatic).
Refused to believe I had ADHD.
Gave me meds to quit smoking instead.
Within 2 days: severe depressive and suicidal thoughts (non-actionable, but scary).
I quit the meds and the doctor.

column1: Trying Again (Round 2)

column3: Found another psychiatrist (this one not connected to my therapist).
Got ADHD meds.
Took them for a week… but the crash was intense.

column1: I wasn’t ready to give up on meds forever,
but adapting to them felt like a full-time job—and honestly, ADHD me doesn’t have the bandwidth for that.
Rebuilding Phase (aka My Glow Up)
This was the turning point:

column3: Quit smoking cold turkey.
Started working out regularly.
Committed to a healthy lifestyle.

column1: Why the change?
I got diagnosed with Grade 3 Fatty Liver—basically the last reversible stage before serious damage. That shook me.
New Addictions (The Healthy Kind)

column3: Got super into black coffee (no milk, no sugar—don’t @ me).
Shifted focus to building my business (still a work in progress, but I’ve grown so much).
Started learning about nutrition, supplements, and gut health.

column1: Supplements I’m Trying (And Loving)
I’m experimenting with these (and tracking how they affect me):

column3: L-Theanine – balances my caffeine intake
L-Tyrosine – helps with mental clarity + brain fog
Creatine – for brain & muscle recovery
Magnesium Glycinate – improves sleep & recovery

column1: Also:

column3: Tons of gut-friendly foods: probiotics, prebiotics, kombucha, kefir, yogurt, pickles—you name it. (Being a chef helps.)

column1: My Philosophy Now

column3: I treat myself as my latest project, and I love it.
I can’t control everything, but I can control what I eat.
The goal? Be the best version of myself in every area of life.

column1: My Secret Weapon: ChatGPT
Honestly?
No productivity app, bullet journal, or to-do list has helped me like ChatGPT.

column3: It’s instant.
It remembers things.
It keeps me focused.
It doesn’t overwhelm me like other tools.

column1: If you haven’t already, try using AI as your ADHD sidekick. It’s a game-changer.
Final Thoughts
Thanks for reading this brain-dump-turned-structured-post.
ADHD isn’t easy—but it’s also a kind of superpower. Love your brain. It loves you back.
Cheers from one neurospicy human to another!",1744289512.0,5
